findings.evidence:
The `api_tokens` table holds `user_id`, `token` and `created_at`; the
middleware looks a request's token up with `WHERE token = $1`. Storing the
token as given keeps the lookup a simple indexed equality.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Tokens are stored as given
findings.recommendation: Store only a hash of the token (SHA-256 of the 32 random bytes is enough for a high-entropy secret; no bcrypt needed) in a `token_hash` column, and have the middleware hash the presented bearer value and look it up with `WHERE token_hash = $1` — still an indexed equality, so the performance argument holds. Anyone who reads the `api_tokens` table (a database backup, a read replica, a support SQL console, an SQL injection elsewhere) otherwise obtains every user's working bearer credential and can call the API as them; since revocation is a Non-Goal, a leaked token cannot even be invalidated. Update the decision, the migration task 1.1 and add a scenario stating the token is not stored in recoverable form (CWE-312, CWE-256).
findings.title: API tokens are stored in clear in the database

findings.evidence:
To diagnose integration problems, the middleware logs each request's
method, path and headers at `info` level, including `Authorization`, so
support can see which token an integration sent.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Every request is logged with its headers
findings.recommendation: Redact `Authorization` (and `Cookie`) before logging: log the scheme and, at most, a non-secret identifier such as the token's id or the first few characters of its hash. As designed, every authenticated request writes a live bearer token to the logs, so anyone with access to the logs or the log pipeline (support, a log aggregation vendor, a leaked log archive) can replay it and act as the user — with no revocation to stop it. The same line would also log Basic-auth passwords that integrations send today. Change task 1.3 so `logs_requests` asserts the header value is absent from the log output (CWE-532).
findings.title: The Authorization header, carrying the bearer token, is logged at info level
